guarantees.claim: When key_len_i == AES_128, rot_word_in[s] is key_i[s][3] for CIPH_FWD and default op_i, and spec_in_128[s] for CIPH_INV.
When key_len_i == AES_256, rot_word_in[s] is key_i[s][7] for CIPH_FWD and default op_i, and key_i[s][3] for CIPH_INV.
When key_len_i == AES_192, AES192Enable==1, and op_i==CIPH_FWD, rot_word_in[s] = (rnd_type[0] || rnd_type[2]) ? key_i[s][5] : (rnd_type[3] ? spec_in_192[s] : key_i[s][3]).
When key_len_i == AES_192, AES192Enable==1, and op_i==CIPH_INV, rot_word_in[s] = rnd_type[2] ? key_i[s][1] : key_i[s][3].
When key_len_i == AES_192 and AES192Enable==0, rot_word_in[s] = key_i[s][3] regardless of op_i.
When key_len_i is AES_128 or AES_192 (with AES192Enable=1) and op_i is not CIPH_FWD nor CIPH_INV, rot_word_in[s] = key_i[s][3].
guarantees.cond: (key_len_i==AES_128 or (key_len_i==AES_192 and AES192Enable)) and op_i not CIPH_FWD/CIPH_INV

guarantees.claim: When key_len_i is AES_256 and op_i is not CIPH_FWD nor CIPH_INV, rot_word_in[s] = key_i[s][7].
When key_len_i is any value other than AES_128, AES_192, or AES_256, rot_word_in[s] = key_i[s][3].

assumptions.claim: Each share of key_i must provide at least 8 words (indices 0 through 7) to avoid out-of-bounds read when key_len_i selects AES_256 or AES_192.
assumptions.cond: When key_len_i == AES_256 (accessing key_i[s][7]) or AES_192 (accessing up to key_i[s][5]).
assumptions.risk: If the actual key_i width is smaller, out-of-bounds accesses may read X or undefined values, corrupting key expansion and potentially causing security bypass.

assumptions.claim: Parameter AES192Enable must be 1 whenever key_len_i can be set to AES_192 during normal operation.
assumptions.risk: Incorrect key expansion: rot_word_in is forced to key_i[3] irrespective of op_i, producing wrong round keys and breaking cryptographic correctness.

uncertain_points.claim: In AES_256 mode, when op_i takes an illegal value (the default branch), rot_word_in is set to key_i[s][7] without error propagation. It is unclear whether this default should trigger an alert or maintain a safe state.
uncertain_points.cond: key_len_i == AES_256, op_i not CIPH_FWD nor CIPH_INV.
uncertain_points.risk: Silent use of a potentially incorrect key word could produce a predictable or weak expanded key, undermining cipher security.

uncertain_points.claim: In AES_192 CIPH_FWD path, rnd_type[1] is unused, and both rnd_type[0] and rnd_type[2] select key_i[5]. The priority encoding could mask simultaneous assertion of multiple round type bits, potentially hiding a fault.
uncertain_points.risk: A fault setting illegal rnd_type combination may go undetected, leading to use of an admissible but possibly incorrect key word.

uncertain_points.claim: With AES192Enable=0 and key_len_i=AES_192, rot_word_in is forced to key_i[3]. It is unknown whether this incompatible configuration should be prevented by higher‑level controls or is an acceptable fallback.
uncertain_points.risk: A misconfiguration silently produces wrong round keys, compromising cryptographic correctness and potentially security.

uncertain_points.claim: The chunk accesses key_i[s] with indices up to 7. If the actual key_i bus width for each share is less than 8 words (due to parameterization), out-of-bounds reads can occur, possibly disclosing adjacent secret state or causing synthesis/simulation mismatches.
uncertain_points.cond: When key_len_i selects an index beyond the supplied key_i width.
uncertain_points.risk: Out-of-bounds access may leak secret material from neighboring registers or produce X‑propagation, leading to exploitable undefined behavior.
